# specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md

```markdown
> For agentic workers: REQUIRED SKILL: derive-roadmap — resume via its
> reconcile step; route each unticked stage per its ROUTING line; never plan
> this document wholesale.

# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md (PROPOSED; covers O1 only, and its §2.2 puts O2 and O3 out of its scope), specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md (Proposed).
Choices made: Python 3.14 in the uv workspace of four packages (from the repository scaffold). No platform is chosen; the ADR's Azure choice is still Proposed.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 136 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second; SEC full-index and daily-index directories |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks of downloading for the full history at 3 requests/second; index row count times request rate, not yet measured |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until the submissions are on disk; measured by Stage 3 |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Filing-index table
      Objective: Ingest every quarterly index and the daily indexes since the latest closed quarter into one filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing beyond the package scaffolds
      Produces: the filing-index table with each filing's archive path; SEC fetching with an identifying User-Agent at no more than 3 requests/second; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: one table holds the rows of every quarterly index from 1993 Q1 to the latest closed quarter plus the daily indexes since, with row counts per quarter and every unparsed file listed; the findings file records the real run's elapsed time, bytes downloaded, row count and request rate.
      Leaves out: manifest and provenance (Stage 4); point-in-time reconciliation (Stage 5); full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submission download
      Objective: Download the submissions that the filing-index table names, resumably.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table and SEC fetching
      Produces: submissions on disk, addressable by archive path; a list of failed or pending downloads
      Exit: every submission the table names for one complete quarter is on disk or listed as failed, and a stopped full-history run resumes without re-downloading finished files; the measured bytes and hours per quarter are recorded.
      Leaves out: manifest and provenance (Stage 4); point-in-time reconciliation (Stage 5); full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submissions on disk; Stage 1's table for form types
      Produces: extracted 10-K and 8-K main documents, each linked to its index row
      Exit: for one complete quarter, every 10-K and 8-K the table names has its main document extracted or is listed as failed with a reason; the measured extraction time and output size are recorded.
      Leaves out: manifest and provenance (Stage 4); point-in-time reconciliation (Stage 5); full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifest and provenance
      Objective: Record what each source file, submission and output came from, so outputs replay from stored bytes without re-downloading.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening: manifest and provenance)
      Consumes: Stages 1–3's outputs
      Produces: a manifest of sources, content hashes and processing versions; retained original bytes; replay from storage
      Exit: a parser-version change rebuilds the index table and the extracted documents from stored bytes with zero SEC requests, and every output row names its source file and hash.
      Leaves out: point-in-time reconciliation (Stage 5); full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Point-in-time reconciliation
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, record additions, changes and withdrawals, and publish versioned generations without discarding history.
      Outcomes: O1 (hardening: point-in-time reconciliation)
      Consumes: Stage 4's manifest and replay
      Produces: versioned table generations behind an active pointer; per-generation change records
      Exit: a re-read quarter with changed content publishes a new generation with its change record while the prior generation stays readable, and a quarter whose new snapshot removes rows does not publish until approved.
      Leaves out: full validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full validation suite
      Objective: Cover the historical index formats, malformed sources and failure paths with committed fixtures that run in CI without SEC access.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening: full validation suite)
      Consumes: Stages 1–5's code
      Produces: golden fixtures and fault-injection tests run in CI
      Exit: CI passes on fixtures covering every index format in the ingested range, HTML-in-place-of-index, truncated downloads and interrupted runs, with no network access.
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run daily ingestion and reconciliation on a schedule on the chosen platform, with one shared SEC request budget and monitoring.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening: scheduling and deployment)
      Consumes: Stages 1–6
      Produces: deployed scheduled runs, alerts and runbooks
      Exit: two consecutive scheduled daily runs and one scheduled reconciliation complete on their own, with their reports recorded, and concurrent runs never exceed the shared request rate.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run SKILL.md §6 over the Outcomes list above: one verdict per outcome with evidence (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries). Each unmet outcome exits as a new stage or as a deferral with a written why.
```

**Message:** Here is the roadmap: Stages 1–3 follow your order; Stages 4–7 are new hardening stages (manifest and provenance, point-in-time reconciliation, full validation suite, scheduling and deployment), which my earlier message should have flagged. Do you approve this partition as written, or do you want to change it?
